lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: similarity as a sequence of transformations
lessonRef.title: Guided practice A: similarity as a sequence of transformations

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Use this example as the model for the guided set below.

items.prompt: Dilate (3, −2) about the origin by factor 4.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: A figure is dilated so that a side of length 6 becomes a side of length 24. What is the scale factor, and what happens to the figure's area?
choices: scale factor 18; the area is multiplied by 16
scale factor 4; the area is multiplied by 16
scale factor 1/4; the area is multiplied by 16
scale factor 4; the area is multiplied by 4

items.prompt: Triangle ABC has ∠A = 59° and ∠B = 43°. Triangle DEF has ∠D = 59° and ∠E = 43°. Are the triangles similar, and on what grounds?
choices: Yes, by AA similarity: two pairs of congruent angles force the third pair to be congruent as well.
No; angle information alone never establishes similarity.
Yes, by SSS similarity.
Yes, but only if a pair of corresponding sides is also known to be congruent.

items.prompt: Under a dilation, a line that does not pass through the centre of dilation …
choices: is mapped to a parallel line
is mapped to a perpendicular line
is mapped to a line with slope multiplied by the scale factor
is mapped onto itself

items.prompt: Dilate the point (6, -6) about the origin with scale factor 2. Give the image.
A figure is dilated so that a side of length 2 becomes a side of length 6. What is the scale factor, and what happens to the figure's area?
choices: scale factor 3; the area is multiplied by 3
scale factor 1/3; the area is multiplied by 9
scale factor 4; the area is multiplied by 9
scale factor 3; the area is multiplied by 9

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Triangle ABC has ∠A = 64° and ∠B = 55°. Triangle DEF has ∠D = 64° and ∠E = 55°. Are the triangles similar, and on what grounds?
choices: Yes, by SSS similarity.
Yes, by AA similarity: two pairs of congruent angles force the third pair to be congruent as well.
No; angle information alone never establishes similarity.
Yes, but only if a pair of corresponding sides is also known to be congruent.

items.prompt: Under a dilation, a segment not through the centre, under a dilation with scale factor k …
choices: is mapped to a parallel segment k times as long
is mapped to a perpendicular segment k times as long
is mapped to a segment k² times as long
is mapped to a segment of the same length

items.prompt: Dilate the point (5, 5) about the origin with scale factor 4. Give the image.

sections.title: Mastery check
